articles.title: Ashiana Housing JV buys 10-acre land in Chennai for senior living project, eyes Rs 1,100 cr revenue
articles.desc: Ashiana Housing Ltd recently revealed its acquisition of nearly 10 acres in Chennai aimed at a senior living initiative. In collaboration with Arihant Foundations, the project estimates a saleable area of around 9 lakh square feet, with an anticipated revenue potential of Rs 1,100 crore. The land purchase cost remains undisclosed, furthering Ashiana's commitment to senior living and group housing developments across various regions.

articles.title: Greaves Electric targets 2x sales volume for Ampere escooter in FY27
articles.desc: "We have seen strong growth in this financial year, with registrations growing 92% year-on-year till October. Registrations in FY27 so far are over 72,000 units, exceeding the 62,644 units registered last financial year," Greaves Electric MD Vikas Singh told PTI in an interview on Thursday.

articles.title: Germany and Austria call for European ownership of TikTok
articles.desc: Germany and Austria on Thursday called for TikTok's European business to be placed under European ownership and control, arguing that regulation alone cannot address concerns over data access and algorithms. In a joint statement, the two politicians called for "a European ownership structure for TikTok's European business and European responsibility for the key technological infrastructure -- from the recommendation algorithm to data access".

articles.title: Capital goods, strategic manufacturing sectors to generate 50 lakh jobs over next five years: CGSSC
articles.desc: The Capital Goods & Strategic Skill Council emphasized the projected creation of 50 lakh job opportunities in India. These jobs will primarily be in capital goods and strategic manufacturing sectors over the next five years. There is a significant demand for skilled workers in various technical roles such as riggers and CNC operators. Advanced manufacturing and automation training are crucial to meet this demand effectively.

articles.title: Millions of people to see average monthly mortgage payments rise by £100
articles.desc: More people face higher mortgage repayments when they roll off a fixed deal than previously estimated.

articles.title: India to cross $1 trillion export mark by March 2027 despite proposed 25% US tariff: ASSOCHAM Secretary General
articles.desc: Speaking to on the sidelines of ASSOCHAM's India Energy Sovereignty Summit 2026, ASSOCHAM Secretary General Saurabh Sanyal expressed confidence in India's export performance, highlighting that the country's exports have already crossed USD 500 billion and are growing at a rate of 15 per cent.

articles.title: India bonds tumble as Brent tops $95 per barrel, RBI flags food inflation risks
articles.desc: Indian government bonds experienced a decline as oil prices increased due to geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. The Reserve Bank of India emphasized broad-based food inflation pressures, complicating the economic landscape. Retail inflation had already surpassed the RBI's threshold of 6% in October, prompting concern among economists. Market participants are anticipating the upcoming monetary policy decision on December 4.

articles.title: NSE among 6 stocks hitting 52-week highs; stock rallies up to 35% in a month
articles.desc: Six BSE 100 stocks, including NSE, DLF and Prestige Estates, hit fresh 52-week highs on Thursday. NSE led monthly gains, surging 35%, followed by Prestige Estates at 32%.

articles.title: Even 17% tariff under India-US trade deal may offer little competitive advantage to Indian exporters: FIEO
articles.desc: Ajay Sahai from the Federation of Indian Export Organisations expressed concerns about a potential BTA with the US. He mentioned that even a 17 per cent tariff concession may not give Indian exporters an advantage. Competing nations, particularly in Southeast Asia, could secure better trade terms through their own agreements. Sahai estimated an 8 per cent additional cost burden for exporters if US tariffs rise to 25 per cent.

articles.title: Nitin Gadkari announces Rs 1 lakh crore road projects for Bengal, promises 250-km Kolkata ring road
articles.desc: Declaring that the Centre would back Bengal's infrastructure push with all necessary financial resources, Gadkari said projects worth around Rs 40,000 crore had already been completed in the state, while works worth Rs 35,000 crore, covering approximately 450 km, were under implementation.

articles.title: Spike in oil prices partly reverses rupee rally, forward premiums surge
articles.desc: The Indian rupee has faced depreciation as a result of escalating oil prices combined with pressures from surrounding currencies. With Brent crude exceeding $96 per barrel, worries about India's import costs and inflation have intensified. Recent days have seen heightened hedging activity among importers, leading analysts to forecast potential testing of the rupee's support levels. Additionally, banks are urging central bank intervention to manage the growing dollar surplus.

articles.title: India attracts $31 bn in climate equity funding, but $22-24 trn needed by 2070: BCG-IVCA
articles.desc: India has secured nearly USD 31 billion in climate funding since 2021, focusing primarily on power and transport. Underfunded sectors such as manufacturing, waste management, and agriculture require significant investment to meet future goals. The country needs approximately USD 22 trillion in total investment by 2070 to support climate transition. Improving investment viability through innovative financing structures has been identified as a crucial step.

articles.title: Govt projects Kharif foodgrain production at 167.14 mln tonnes despite El Nino; 2025-26 crop output a record
articles.desc: Kharif foodgrain production for the 2026-27 crop year is projected at 167.14 million tonnes amid weather challenges. Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan announced these estimates despite El Nino and a delayed monsoon. In the previous crop year, foodgrain production reached a record high of 378.54 million tonnes. Additionally, pulses and oilseeds are being prioritized due to India's reliance on imports.

articles.title: How Donald Trump's proposed fresh tariff salvo for India compare with rival nations
articles.desc: The US has proposed a 25% tariff on Indian imports to address excess industrial capacity issues. This rate could decrease to 17% if a trade deal is reached. India's trade ministry is reviewing the US's trade practices allegations while defending its own situation. Trade talks have been prolonged due to various complications, including tariff laws and military incidents.

articles.desc: SoftBank's five-year credit default swap spread, which measures the cost of insuring its bonds, widened more than 20 basis points to 534.6 bps, a four-year high. SoftBank's default probability sat at 34.8%.

articles.title: Rupee falls 20 paise to 92.40 against US dollar in early trade
articles.desc: The rupee fell 20 paise to 92.40 against the US dollar in early trade. Higher crude oil prices and proposed tariffs by the US administration increased dollar demand. Foreign fund inflows supported the rupee but it faced pressure from rising crude prices. The US proposed 25 percent tariffs on imports from India, which raised inflation concerns. India rejected these allegations and expressed commitment to finalize a bilateral trade deal.

articles.title: Why is SanDisk stock falling despite surging profits?
articles.desc: SanDisk shares tumble amid fading AI optimism, declining NAND price forecasts and semiconductor sector weakness. Despite strong earnings and data centre demand, investors fear potential memory-chip oversupply and weakening future profitability.

articles.title: Adani firms plan public bond sale to raise at least Rs 2,000 crore
articles.desc: Adani Enterprises and Adani Power are planning public bond offerings to raise at least Rs 20 billion ($220 million), according to sources. The fundraising could help revive India's subdued public debt market, where issuances have lagged the previous fiscal year's levels. Both companies are working with local bond arrangers.

articles.desc: SpaceX said earlier in the day it would contribute one newly issued share of its Class A common stock to every currently active Trump Account, adding that Musk will personally match the number of shares donated by the company.

articles.title: Anthropic chief Dario Amodei denies wanting humans to 'surrender' free will to AI
articles.desc: Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei on Wednesday denied wanting humanity to give up its free will to AI, calling it "absurd" to attribute the idea to him as rival tech leaders push back. "No, I do not believe that we should 'surrender human free will' to AI systems, and it's absurd to suggest that I do," Amodei wrote in a lengthy post on X, a week after Anthropic's record-setting stock market debut.

articles.desc: The company plans to kick off the efforts in the first three months of 2027, the people said, asking not to be identified as the information isn’t public. Discussions are preliminary, though some investors are pushing for the process to start sooner, they said.

articles.title: Data centre rush drives biggest rise in Australian business investment since mining boom
articles.desc: Australian business investment surged anew in the September quarter as firms poured money into data centres, recording its biggest rise since 2011 at the height of the mining boom, while companies further upgraded spending plans for coming months.

articles.title: OpenAI taps Cravath litigator for court showdown with Musk over AI dominance
articles.desc: OpenAI said Cravath's Gary Bornstein, co-head of the New York firm's litigation department, will be lead trial counsel in federal court in Fort Worth, where the case is set to be heard by a jury in March.

articles.title: Robots roam Singapore's urban AI testing ground
articles.desc: When coffee is spilled at an office block in a futuristic enclave of Singapore, AI-powered cameras and sensors detect it and send a cleaning robot right away. A district-wide "open digital platform" coordinates the robots and connects different locations, gathering data from thousands of cameras and sensors on everything from air temperature to foot traffic.
